chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, raising it, said:

When the people wake up in the morning fasting, and they had not seen the crescent, and there come a group of just people testifying upon the sighting, so let them break the Fast, and let them go out from the next day, at the beginning of the day, to their Eid.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if people start fasting but the crescent is not seen until ahs been sighted by a reliable group?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'following the majority' in lunar calendar calculations, prioritizing communal testimony over individual observation to ensure unity in worship. It specifically addresses the scenario where the community has already begun fasting based on a general assumption, requiring them to break their fast and proceed to Eid prayer upon credible witness testimony, even if the sighting occurs after dawn. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical jurisprudence (fiqh) that balances religious obligation with social cohesion and ease for the believers.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, raising it, said,

‘When the people wake up in the morning Fasting, and they had not seen the crescent, and there come a group of just people testifying upon the sighting, so let them break the Fast, and let them go out from the next day, at the beginning of the day, to their Eid’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If people are fasting and have not seen the new moon, then a just people come and testify to their seeing the new moon they must discontinue fasting and on the morning of the next day come out for their ‘Id.’”
